headline: Across media, gaming, publishing, and education, companies show mixed financial performance but a clear trend toward expanding IT spend.
summary: Media firms like Disney and Versant report revenue growth and increased operating margins, while gaming players such as Bally’s see revenue gains but margin pressure. Publishing and education sectors face revenue misses and operational losses, yet some entities are pursuing acquisitions and digital platform upgrades. IT investment remains a common theme, with most companies expanding spend to support AI, platform rebuilds, and new technology partnerships.

industries.summary: Disney and Versant posted revenue growth and higher operating margins, indicating healthy financials. WBD/Skydance raised its EBITDA outlook despite a revenue decline, showing confidence in future earnings. Cox Communications signals growth through AI platform integration and a large acquisition.

leaders.why: Revenue up 7% and operating income up 21%

themes.title: AI & Tech Investment
themes.detail: Disney bid $20 million for AI assets; Cox integrated AI platform into CRM.

themes.title: Platform Rebuild
themes.detail: WBD/Skydance consolidated streaming stacks; Versant expanded Fandango and CNBC platforms.

industries.it_note: Companies are investing in AI, platform consolidation, and new tech assets to drive growth.

industries.summary: Bally’s achieved 20% revenue growth but a negative margin, driven by strong B2C and North America Interactive performance. Caesars reported modest revenue with a net loss, while Brightstar and Light & Wonder had stable or slightly negative margins. The sector shows investment in automation and new technology solutions.

themes.title: Automation & Platform
themes.detail: Bally’s automation initiatives improve profitability; new lottery tech contracts expand reach.

themes.title: M&A
themes.detail: Bally’s acquired evoke plc to strengthen sports betting.

industries.it_note: Gaming firms are spending on automation, platform upgrades, and new vendor contracts to stay competitive.

industries.summary: Scholastic missed revenue targets and widened its operating loss, while other publishers lack recent data. The only notable activity is Scholastic’s acquisition of Cottage Door Press for $71 million.

themes.title: Acquisition
themes.detail: Scholastic bought Cottage Door Press to diversify content.

industries.it_note: Limited information on IT spending; likely constrained by financial performance.

industries.summary: Key educational institutions received grants and formed AI partnerships, but no financial metrics are available. The focus appears to be on research and technology collaboration rather than commercial performance.

themes.title: AI Collaboration
themes.detail: NYU and SLU partnered with technology firms to expand AI initiatives.

industries.it_note: IT investment is driven by research grants and partnership agreements, with no clear spend trend.
